objectClass.notes: Static single-storey branded retail box on thaikit's shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: glazing is a tinted mostly-opaque pane, not an opening. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. Distinguishing features on this plate: grey concrete-render walls carrying rain streaking off the coping; a bright YELLOW fascia lightbox in a dark border filling the front parapet's whole face under ONE continuous coping ring; a yellow shopfront surround with a projecting lintel over a nearly full-width glazed front; a yellow delivery counter whose worktop passes OUT through a hatch in the glazing; a hinged entrance door on the right with a pull-handle plate on its leading edge; a LARGE corrugated roller shutter with guide channels and a proud hood filling most of the +X wall; and two packaged rooftop units with louvred fan grilles. No entrance canopy. THIRD BUILD, on the owner's brief (2026-09-01): the glazing is plain tinted glass with NO interior image, the delivery hatch is a real 0.62 m opening into a dark room, the wordmark is a nano-banana-2 generated mark, both rooftop units stand square at the back of the roof with no duct kerb, the shutter is centred on its wall under a deeper hood flush with its guides, and the yellow surround, the cast stone and the galvanised plant carry weathering tiles with the counter pinned clean. Where the brief and the plate disagree the brief wins and the departure is recorded.

The plate's glazing shows a parcel-shop interior. On the brief NONE of it ships: the second build projected the rectified plate over the panes and the owner rejected it ("those textures don't work, I just want glass there"). The glazing is plain tinted plate glass, #6f8a8c at opacity 0.90 and roughness 0.12, over a DARK backdrop slab 4 mm off the shell face -- one box folded into the roof-deck submission with a vertex tone of 0x9a9a9a -- so the panes look into a dim room rather than at the render wall. Measured at azimuth 0: glass luma 141, hatch 74, both clear of the backdrop's 58.

The delivery counter is the ONE piece of the interior that is real geometry, because in the plate its worktop passes OUT through a hatch in the glazing. The worktop is at the plate's counter height (1.10 m; rectified row 450 of 678 reads 1.14) and the hatch is a REAL OPENING the width of the middle bay, 0.62 m tall from the worktop to its own head rail at 1.72, with the transom rail stopping either side of the bay. The plate's own opening is 0.31 m under a continuous transom; it is enlarged on the brief so it reads as the hole customers pass money and parcels through.

The S in FLASH is a LIGHTNING BOLT in the plate, and it is WHITE with a thin black outline, not black. The second build set FLA / bolt / H / EXPRESS from a font by measured boxes and the bolt's tail ran through the E of EXPRESS. The mark is now GENERATED by nano-banana-2 (a flat front-on graphic on the fascia yellow, scratch/_flash/nb_sign.png), its glyph group cut out by colour distance from the generated yellow, snapped to the exact #FFF600, and placed at the SAME measured position on the 2048x320 band -- u 0.233..0.626, v 0.157..0.882, aspect preserved -- so EXPRESS sits right-aligned under the H with clear yellow between it and the bolt. Baked as a WebP data URI; the canvas ops remain as the decode fallback only.

The roller shutter is authored as 40 half-round beads, not flat slats: the plate's rib pitch is 7.3 px against 118.6 px/m at that column, i.e. 62 mm over a 2.70 m opening, and its slats read as alternating bright and dark stripes, which is a curved surface catching the key light. Guide channels, a bottom rail and a proud hood are separate geometry.

Two elevations of the plate were measured through a PROJECTIVE map rather than by eye, and the plate turned out to be projectively INCONSISTENT -- its base line, its fascia band and its parapet coping do not agree on one vanishing point. The front is therefore rectified on the two lines that DO agree (the base line and the fascia band, to 0.03 px/px) and the side is measured through a map fitted to the side base line and the side coping line. Where the two disagree the divergence is under 0.2 m and the declared module decides.

The rooftop units are the plate's packaged type: a recessed louvre grille with the fan disc visible behind it, a flanged lid with a round cowl opening, and two panel seams down the long side. All of it merges into the ONE instanced geometry, so the second unit costs nothing. On the brief both stand SQUARE to the building (the plate turns the right one a little) at the back of the roof, z -2.05, and the low duct kerb the second build ran between them is gone. Their casing carries a galvanised spangle tile generated by nano-banana-2, made seamless and normalised into multiplier space, and the grille's back plate, fan disc and blades are toned by a vertex colour on the plant material so the intake reads dark behind lighter blades.

The shutter hood is FLUSH with the outer faces of the guide channels and 0.50 m tall, standing 0.28 m proud of the wall, on the brief; its outer face at x 4.22 is 0.22 m past the parapet plane, a 2.75 % overrun of the declared width on one axis and inside the 10 % tolerance.

silhouette.description: One rectangular prism. The silhouette events are the fascia lightbox standing proud of the parapet in its dark border, the yellow lintel cantilevering over the glazing, the shutter hood standing 0.28 m proud of the +X wall, flush with the shutter guides, the delivery counter's worktop passing out through an open hatch in the glazing, and the two rooftop units breaking the roofline against the coping at the back of the roof.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -4.00..+4.00 (parapet ring outer faces) = 8.00. y spans 0.00..4.60 = 4.60. z spans -3.50 (rear parapet) ..+3.50 = 7.00. The shell front face is set back to z=+2.50 so anything cantilevering off it lands ON the declared depth rather than overrunning it.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to w:h:d = 1 : 0.739 : 0.832 against the declared 1 : 0.575 : 0.875 -- 29% taller and 5% shallower. The plate's own building is visibly tall and narrow; the declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m is the KIT's shared retail module across seven siblings, so the declaration wins and the divergence is reported. It has one consequence worth naming: the plate's rooftop plant stands well ABOVE its coping, and an 8 x 4.6 envelope whose top IS the coping cannot carry that. The roof deck is raised inside the parapet ring instead (3.80..3.92 rather than 3.50..3.62) so the units stand on a shallow roof rather than in a 0.8 m pit, which is the part of the plate's reading that the envelope does not forbid.

componentTree.name: Building shell
componentTree.topologyRationale: One continuous render skin over four walls. Splitting it per elevation would cost a draw call per wall for the life of the prop to express one material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Solid box, x -3.94..+3.94, y 0..3.55, z -3.44..+2.50. SOLID, not a ring: the prop is an exterior shell only ever seen from outside, so an interior would cost draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Solid also means the shopfront needs no opening cut in it, which removes all four reveal faces and the z-fighting they cause.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Set 0.06 m INSIDE the parapet ring on every elevation (walls at +-3.94 and -3.44; parapet at +-4.00 and -3.50). That difference is a coping drip edge, and it is what stops a wall face and a parapet face being coplanar and co-facing.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Grey concrete render, roughness 0.90 -- rougher than the painted siblings, because this plate shows bare board-marked concrete rather than a paint film. pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: base-center, as the asset declares. A STATIC exterior shell: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the building, not with its canopy plates.

componentTree.name: Roof deck
componentTree.topologyRationale: A flat deck plane. Its own component only because the membrane is a visibly different value from the wall render, and this prop is seen from above in every hero shot.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Thin slab spanning y 3.50..3.62, overlapping UNDER the parapet ring.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Spans y 3.50..3.62 so its underside is sunk INTO the shell rather than resting on it. Authored flush, the deck bottom face and the parapet ring bottom face would both sit at y=3.550 facing down -- tens of square metres of coplanar co-facing surface, and exactly the pair check-coplanar catches.

localFeatures.description: recessed louvre grille with the fan disc behind

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Dark deck membrane, roughness 0.93. Raised to y 3.80..3.92 inside the parapet ring so the rooftop plant stands on a shallow roof rather than down in a 0.8 m pit, and the units then break the roofline the way the plate's do. Source component for the rooftop-unit instancing system. Also carries the dark BACKDROP SLAB behind the glazed opening (X -3.16..+2.94, Y 0.29..2.62, z 3.142..3.150), folded into the same submission with a vertex tone of 0x9a9a9a on a white deck, so the panes and the hatch look into a dim room.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Parapet ring and fascia wall
componentTree.topologyRationale: A continuous upstand ring in one material, with the front simply taller -- which a plan extrusion cannot express, since an extrude carries one height. Merged boxes are the right primitive, and anything else in the same material folds in here rather than costing its own submission.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Front fascia wall plus left, right and rear upstands, merged into ONE component and ONE draw call, with same-material cladding folded in.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Parapet outer faces stand 0.06 m PROUD of the shell walls. Authored flush they would be coplanar and co-facing along all three elevations. The front box overlaps into the shell volume rather than butting it.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Primitive is "box" because the schema enumerates primitives, but this is a MERGED cluster built into one BufferGeometry and submitted as ONE draw call.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The SAME render as the shell -- one material, and the same tile. The first backdrop tone (0x606060) rendered the hatch near black -- a hole to the gate and to a viewer -- and 0x9a9a9a puts it at 74, dark enough to read as an opening beside the 141 glass and clear of the backdrop band. Scored 0.90 and not higher because the plate does show an interior and the model, by the brief, shows a dim room and a counter edge.

featureReviews.evidence: 40 half-round beads at 62 mm pitch over a 4.44 x 2.70 m opening at Z -2.37..+2.07, centred on the +X wall, between two guide channels, over a bottom rail and under a 0.50 m hood flush with the guides' outer faces and 0.28 m proud of the wall. Galvanised spangle tile at 1.4 m over beads and guides; galv albedo #d8dfe5 = #b6bcc1 / the tile's 0.841 mean multiplier.
featureReviews.notes: Width and pitch are the plate's measurements; the placement is the brief's (the plate has the opening 0.46 m toward the front). The hood was the visible defect: a thin lip 0.44 m longer than the guides, reading as an overhang past the door. It is now the plate's box hood, and the grime tile on the cast stone puts the streaking the owner named on it.

featureReviews.evidence: Two packaged units, 1.34 x 0.90 x 0.88 m, both square to the building at x +-1.50, z -2.05, one instanced geometry: casing in the generated galvanised spangle, the grille's back plate 0x4a4e52 and fan disc 0x3c4044 behind blades at 0xa8acb0 by vertex colour, flanged lid, cowl, seams and feet. The duct kerb between them is gone.
featureReviews.notes: The owner named three things -- one unit yawed, debris beside it, both to go to the back -- and a fourth, that the casings looked flat. The yaw and the kerb were the plate's, and the brief overrides them. The texture is nano-banana-2's galvanised sheet, contrast halved so it reads as zinc mottle rather than marble (the first normalisation clipped 40% of the spangle to white), and the dark tone behind the blades is what finally makes the grille read as an intake instead of a panel of the casing. The units still overrun the declared height by 0.22 m, inside tolerance and deliberate.

featureReviews.evidence: A real leaf on a real hinge at the RIGHT jamb (X +2.89), 1.36 x 2.11 m, with stiles, rails, a plain glazed pane and a vertical pull bar on two stand-offs at X +1.83.
featureReviews.notes: Unchanged apart from the pane, which is now plain glass like the fixed glazing. Hung on the right because the plate's handle plate is on the LEFT of the leaf, the leading edge of a right-hung door. The ONE thing on this prop that moves and the only named pivot beyond the root.

featureReviews.evidence: Pale cast stone (#a9adb1, PBR confidence 0.726) capping front, sides and rear at ONE level, y 4.44..4.60, inset from the parapet faces; the 0.50 m shutter hood flush with the guides; the plinth under the shopfront. One submission, carrying a grime-and-streak tile at 1.6 m.
featureReviews.notes: Grouped by MATERIAL rather than location. The hood's grime is what the brief asked for on the 'silver overhang'; the coping ring takes the same tile, which is where a real coping's streaking starts.

featureReviews.evidence: A seamless 512 tile in MULTIPLIER space -- rain streaking off the coping, patchy float marks, board-marked seams at 1.2 m and fine aggregate speckle -- repeated metrically at 3.2 m over the shell and the parapet. Lit front wall luma 193 against the plate's 193.
featureReviews.notes: Unchanged from the second build. Procedural, so the marks are the right kind and strength and not in the plate's own places.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93, up from 0.91. 3528/16000 triangles, 13/16 draw calls, 8/8 materials, 13/32 unique geometries, 5 textures at 8.7 MB. Every critical feature is at or above its threshold. The owner's seven items are all on the model: plain glass, a generated mark with no bolt/E overlap, an open hatch, square units at the back with no debris, a centred shutter under a flush box hood, textured plant, and wear on the lintel and hood with the counter clean. Residuals: the harness rig is not the plate's studio light, the render and wear tiles are procedural, and the plate's interior is by choice not shown.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Two repetition systems collapse 3 parts into 2 submissions; 43 shutter pieces fold into one component, six stone runs into another, five yellow boxes into a third and 30 pieces of rooftop unit into one instanced geometry. Thirteen of sixteen draw calls, the two spare over the first build being the hinged door leaf, which is the one thing here that moves.

materials.note: Eight of eight materials, unchanged even though the prop carries FIVE post-construction images: a canvas assigned AFTER material construction costs a texture, not a material. wall covers shell and parapet and carries the render tile; yellow covers surround, lintel and counter and carries the wear tile with the counter pinned clean; frame covers the shopfront framing, the lightbox border and the door leaf; glass covers the fixed glazing and the door pane, plain; galv covers the shutter and both rooftop units and carries the generated spangle; coping covers the parapet cap, the hood and the plinth and carries the grime tile; deck carries the backdrop slab by vertex tone. fascia duplicates yellow ONLY because it carries the wordmark image. Two materials run vertexColors (deck, galv), and every mesh on them has a colour attribute, white where untinted.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: Triangles are NOT the binding constraint on this prop -- draw calls are. The headroom is deliberately spent on silhouette quality (chamfers, cowl segments, shutter ribs) and must not be read as room to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: box, cylinder and merged-box clusters only. No organic surfaces exist on this subject.

Two InstancedMesh systems carry 3 of the discrete parts. The 40-bead shutter is a merged component rather than a system because the beads share one submission with the guides and the bottom rail, which are not repeats of anything.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. The brand fascia receives its wordmark as a generated canvas assigned AFTER material construction -- the documented route for a printed brand fascia, unaffected by the declaration.

risks.description: Rear and left elevations are not in the single plate; authored plain.
The shopfront frame ships at #6B6F6C rather than its measured #4F5352.
risks.mitigation: Forced by the harness: at the measured value the frame renders at the backdrop luma and the mullion lattice reads as a hole. Recorded on the material with the measurement it departs from.

risks.description: The glazing tint is a design value, not a measurement, and it is now the whole of what the panes show.
risks.mitigation: The owner asked for plain glass and rejected the projected interior. The tint is a cool grey-green over a dark backdrop slab, chosen so the panes read as glass into a dim room and measured at luma 141 against the hatch's 74. Recorded as chosen at confidence 0.60.

risks.description: Four things are authored against the plate on the owner's brief: no interior image, a 0.62 m hatch where the plate has 0.31, both rooftop units square and at the back where the plate yaws one near the middle, and the shutter centred where the plate has it 0.46 m toward the front.
risks.mitigation: Each is recorded here with the plate's own measurement beside it; the review scores the build against the brief, and this risk is what stops a later reader "correcting" them back to the plate.

risks.description: The open hatch is a genuinely dark region enclosed by the silhouette.
risks.mitigation: Measured at azimuth 0: hatch luma 74, above the backdrop's 58, so the turntable gate has no band to flood-fill there. The backdrop tone was raised from 0x606060 (which rendered the hatch near black) for exactly this reason.

risks.description: The shutter hood's outer face at x 4.22 overruns the declared 8.00 m width by 0.22 m on one side.
risks.mitigation: 2.75 % on one axis, inside the 10 % tolerance, and it is the one projecting element of that wall -- the plate's own hood stands proud by about this much.

risks.description: The plate's base line, fascia band and parapet coping do not agree on one vanishing point, so no single projective solve fits the whole facade.
risks.mitigation: The rectification is anchored on the two lines that DO agree (base and fascia band, to 0.03 px/px) and the side is measured through its own map. Cross-checked against the near corner found independently as a 20-luma step at plate x=583 in three separate rows. Divergences are under 0.2 m and the declared module decides.

risks.description: At azimuth 90 the troughs between the shutter beads render at the backdrop luma of 58 on isolated single-pixel rows, and the turntable gate flood-fills them as background enclosed by the silhouette.
risks.mitigation: MEASURED, not waved through: every enclosed component is exactly 1.00 px thick (scratch/_holecc.mjs), which is the anti-aliased-edge case --allow-holes exists for. Four remedies were tried and rejected on measurement -- bead radius, burial depth, segment count and a galv albedo lift -- because the flagged rows sit 32 px apart against a 5.5 px rib pitch, so it is a beat against the pixel grid rather than a tone that can be lifted out of the band. Lifting it far enough would need an albedo of 235, which is not a galvanised shutter.

risks.description: The rooftop units reach y 4.82 against a declared 4.60.
risks.mitigation: Inside the asset's own 10 % scale tolerance (4.14..5.06) and deliberate. The BUILDING -- walls, parapet, coping -- is still exactly 4.60 x 8.00 x 7.00; what overruns is plant standing on its roof, which is what the plate shows and what a level editor expects of a rooftop unit.
Sharing is documented per material so a future editor can see what is doubled up.
